text_blocks.snippet: NSAIDs (Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs) are primarily metabolized in the liver through cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes, particularly CYP2C9. These enzymes convert NSAIDs into inactive metabolites, which are then excreted primarily via the kidneys (though some may be excreted in bile). The specific metabolic pathways and the extent of metabolism can vary between different NSAIDs.
